audit_items.proof_trace: The function signature of `reserve.accrue_interest` takes a `reserve_factor` parameter and correctly credits `reserve_factor * interest_accumulated` to `cash_reserve` (reserve.move:143). However, the only caller (`market.move:1025`) passes `asset.repay_fee_rate()` — documented as 'fee rate paid to the protocol in repay' — in place of a separate reserve_factor; `AssetConfig` has no dedicated reserve_factor field. Additionally, `repay_fee_rate` is never applied during actual loan repayments (`handle_repay` calls `reserve.repay_amount(coin)` with no fee deduction), so no repay fee is charged and interest accrual credits only a tiny fraction (e.g., 1 bp) to the treasury instead of the intended reserve factor.
audit_items.attack_scenario: A borrower opens any loan; as time elapses every interaction (borrow, repay, liquidate) triggers `accrue_interest`, which credits `repay_fee_rate * interest` to the protocol treasury rather than the intended `reserve_factor * interest`. With the test-configured rate of 1 basis point versus a typical 1% reserve factor, the protocol treasury receives ~100× less than designed, with the shortfall implicitly benefiting suppliers via higher effective supply yield.
